questions.question: Which explorer sailed west from Spain in 1492 and reached islands in the Americas?
questions.explanation: He hoped to find a sea route to Asia. Instead he landed on islands in the Caribbean that Europeans did not know.

questions.question: Which explorer's expedition was the first to sail all the way around the world?
questions.explanation: Magellan was killed on the way, in 1521. One of his ships, the Victoria, finished the trip in 1522.

questions.question: Which explorer led the first team to reach the South Pole, in 1911?
questions.explanation: Amundsen's team arrived in December 1911. Scott's British team got there about a month later.

questions.question: Which mountain did Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay climb in 1953?
questions.explanation: They were the first people known to stand on top of it. Everest is on the border between Nepal and Tibet.

questions.question: Which explorer from Venice told the story of his travels in Asia in a famous book?
questions.explanation: He left Venice in 1271 with his father and uncle. His book made many Europeans curious about Asia.

questions.question: Which explorer mapped the coast of New Zealand and the east coast of Australia in the 1700s?
questions.explanation: Cook made three long voyages in the Pacific Ocean. His maps were so good that sailors used them for many years.

questions.question: What was the name of the Aztec capital city, built on an island in a lake?
questions.explanation: Long roads called causeways joined the island to the shore. Mexico City was later built on the same place.

questions.question: Which mountain range was the heart of the Inca Empire?
questions.explanation: The Inca built roads and rope bridges over the high mountains. Runners carried messages along the roads.

questions.question: Which people built the mountain city of Machu Picchu?
questions.explanation: Machu Picchu lies high in the Andes mountains of Peru. It was built in the 1400s.

questions.question: Who started the Mongol Empire around the year 1206?
questions.explanation: He joined many tribes into one people. His empire later grew to be one of the biggest land empires ever.

questions.question: Which animal did Mongol warriors ride into battle?
questions.explanation: Each warrior took several horses with him, so he could change to a fresh one. Mongol children learned to ride very young.

questions.question: Vasco da Gama sailed from Portugal around Africa to which country?
questions.explanation: He reached the city of Calicut in 1498. It was the first sea route from Europe to India.

questions.question: Why did Emperor Shah Jahan build the Taj Mahal?
questions.correct: As a tomb for his wife
questions.explanation: His wife Mumtaz Mahal died in 1631. He ruled the Mughal Empire and wanted a beautiful place to remember her.

questions.question: What was the name of Columbus's largest ship on his first trip?
questions.explanation: The Santa María ran onto a reef at Christmas 1492 and was lost. The smaller Niña took Columbus home.

questions.question: What animals pulled Roald Amundsen's sledges to the South Pole?
questions.explanation: Dogs were fast and strong in the cold. Scott's team used ponies and pulled many sledges by hand.

questions.question: What was the ruler of the Ottoman Empire called?
questions.explanation: For centuries the sultans ruled from Constantinople, a city now called Istanbul. The empire lasted for more than 600 years.

questions.question: Which queen ruled Britain from 1837 to 1901, when the British Empire was very big?
questions.explanation: She became queen at 18. In 1876 she also got the title Empress of India.

questions.question: Which continent did the Scottish explorer David Livingstone explore in the 1800s?
questions.explanation: Livingstone was a doctor from Scotland. He crossed Africa and was the first European to see a huge waterfall there.

questions.question: Which animal did the Inca use to carry loads in the mountains?
questions.explanation: Llamas can walk on steep paths and live in thin mountain air. The Inca also used llama wool.

questions.question: Why do people in Brazil speak Portuguese?
questions.explanation: Portuguese ships reached Brazil in 1500. Portugal ruled it until 1822.

questions.question: Which of these foods came to Europe from the Americas after 1492?
questions.explanation: Explorers also brought tomatoes, maize and chocolate. At first many Europeans were afraid to eat potatoes.

questions.question: America is named after the first name of which Italian explorer?
questions.explanation: Vespucci said that the lands in the west were a new continent. A mapmaker put his name on a map in 1507.

questions.question: Magellan named the Pacific Ocean. What does the word Pacific mean?
questions.explanation: His ships found calm water after a hard trip through a stormy strait near the tip of South America. So he called the sea peaceful.

questions.question: What did sailors use to find north when the sky was cloudy?
questions.explanation: A compass needle is a small magnet that turns to point north. This helped explorers to steer far from land.

questions.question: What is the round tent of the Mongol herders called?
questions.explanation: A yurt has a wooden frame covered with felt. It is easy to take down and carry to a new camp.

questions.question: Edmund Hillary, who climbed Mount Everest in 1953, came from which country?
questions.explanation: Hillary was a beekeeper before he became famous. He also helped to build schools in Nepal.

questions.question: How many ships did Columbus have on his first trip across the Atlantic Ocean?
questions.explanation: The ships were the Niña, the Pinta and the Santa María. About 90 men sailed with him.

questions.question: Which continent is the South Pole on?
questions.explanation: Antarctica is covered by thick ice. No one lives there for good, but scientists stay at research stations for a time.

questions.question: Marco Polo travelled from Italy to which far-away country, where he stayed for many years?
questions.explanation: He travelled along the Silk Road. He told Europeans about paper money and other things they had never seen.

questions.question: Which animal did the Spanish bring to the Americas that Native peoples had not seen before?
questions.explanation: Later, many Native peoples learned to ride and used horses for hunting and travel.

questions.question: What is a colony?
questions.correct: A land ruled by a faraway country
questions.explanation: Many European countries had colonies in Africa, Asia and the Americas. Most of them are now independent countries.

questions.question: Which illness did sailors on long trips often get when they had no fresh fruit?
questions.explanation: Scurvy comes from too little vitamin C. Oranges and lemons stopped it, and later sailors took them on board.

questions.question: Zheng He sailed huge ships to Africa in the early 1400s. Which country was he from?
questions.explanation: His fleet had hundreds of ships and thousands of men, far more than Columbus had.

questions.question: In old stories, explorers in South America searched for El Dorado. What was it?
questions.explanation: El Dorado was never found. The stories made many Spanish explorers go deep into the jungle.

questions.question: Which spice did explorers sail to Asia to find, because it sold for a high price in Europe?
questions.explanation: Black pepper grew in southern India. Explorers also looked for cloves and nutmeg from the Spice Islands.

questions.question: Which animal carried goods across the deserts on the Silk Road?
questions.explanation: Camels can walk for days without water. Traders travelled in long groups called caravans.

questions.question: Captain Cook claimed the east coast of Australia in 1770. For which country?
questions.explanation: Cook named the land New South Wales. British ships later brought many settlers there.

questions.question: Akbar and Shah Jahan were emperors of which empire in India?
questions.explanation: The Mughal Empire began in 1526 and lasted until 1857. Its emperors built forts, gardens and the Taj Mahal.

questions.question: Which country did the polar explorer Roald Amundsen come from?
questions.explanation: Amundsen's team were expert skiers, which helped them move fast over the snow and ice.

questions.question: The Aztecs made a drink from which beans?
questions.explanation: The drink was bitter and often had spices in it. Cocoa beans were also used as money.

questions.question: Where did Ferdinand Magellan die in 1521, during his trip around the world?
questions.explanation: He was killed in a fight on the small island of Mactan. His crew went on without him.

questions.question: Ibn Battuta, who travelled over much of Africa and Asia in the 1300s, was born in which country?
questions.explanation: He left his home town of Tangier at 21 and travelled for about 30 years. He told his story in a book.

questions.question: Zheng He led huge fleets across the Indian Ocean in the early 1400s. Which Chinese dynasty did he serve?
questions.explanation: He made seven great voyages between 1405 and 1433. His fleets sailed as far as East Africa.

questions.question: Hernán Cortés and his soldiers defeated which empire in 1521?
questions.explanation: They had help from local peoples who were enemies of the Aztecs. Many people also died from new diseases.

questions.question: Francisco Pizarro captured the ruler Atahualpa in 1532. Which empire did Atahualpa rule?
questions.explanation: The Inca ruler was captured in the town of Cajamarca in Peru. Spain then took control of the Inca lands.

questions.question: Which British explorer reached the South Pole in January 1912 and found that Amundsen had been there first?
questions.explanation: Scott and his four companions died on the way back. Their camp and diaries were found by a search party.

questions.question: What happened to Ernest Shackleton's ship Endurance in 1915?
wrong: It hit a reef near Australia
questions.explanation: The ship got stuck in ice in the Weddell Sea. Everyone on board survived, and the last of them were rescued in 1916.

questions.question: Tenzing Norgay, who climbed Everest with Hillary, belonged to which mountain people?
questions.explanation: Many Sherpas work as mountain guides in Nepal. They are used to living and working at great height.

questions.question: Which Mongol ruler, a grandson of Genghis Khan, became the emperor of China in the 1200s?
questions.explanation: He started the Yuan dynasty and moved his capital to a place now called Beijing.

questions.question: In 1453 Sultan Mehmed II took which city, ending the Byzantine Empire?
questions.explanation: The city is now called Istanbul. Its great walls were hit by very large cannons.

questions.question: Which country's explorers, including Cossacks, crossed Siberia to the Pacific coast in the 1600s?
questions.explanation: Many of them travelled along rivers, because it was easier than walking through the forests. They hunted for valuable furs.

questions.question: Magellan was Portuguese, but which country's king paid for his voyage around the world?
questions.explanation: The King of Portugal said no to his plan. So Magellan went to the Spanish king, who agreed.

questions.question: What was the nickname of Prince Henry of Portugal, who sent ships to explore Africa's coast in the 1400s?
questions.explanation: Henry himself did not sail far. His captains reached Madeira and the Azores, and went far down the coast of West Africa.

questions.question: On which island group did Captain Cook die in 1779?
questions.explanation: Cook was the first European known to visit Hawaii. He died there on his third voyage in the Pacific.

questions.question: Which English sailor went around the world between 1577 and 1580 in the Golden Hind?
questions.explanation: He was the first English captain to sail around the world. Queen Elizabeth I made him a knight.

questions.question: The Bering Strait is named after Vitus Bering. Which country was he born in?
questions.explanation: Bering was born in Horsens. He sailed for the Russian tsar and explored the sea between Asia and Alaska.

questions.question: In 1947 Thor Heyerdahl crossed the Pacific Ocean on a balsa raft with what name?
questions.explanation: He wanted to show that people could have sailed from South America to the Pacific islands in old times.

questions.question: Which Norwegian let his ship Fram freeze into the Arctic ice in 1893, to drift across the sea?
questions.explanation: The drift took almost three years. Nansen and one companion left the ship and went on towards the Pole on skis.

questions.question: In 1488 Bartolomeu Dias sailed past which cape near the southern tip of Africa?
questions.explanation: Dias is said to have called it the Cape of Storms. The King of Portugal gave it a more hopeful name.

questions.question: Which Ottoman sultan, nicknamed 'the Magnificent', ruled in the 1500s?
questions.explanation: He ruled for 46 years, longer than any other Ottoman sultan. In Turkey he is called 'the Lawgiver'.

questions.question: The Spanish conquerors of the Americas, such as Cortés and Pizarro, were called what?
questions.explanation: Conquistador is the Spanish word for conqueror. Many of them hoped to win gold and land.

questions.question: Which country did John Cabot sail for when he reached North America in 1497?
questions.explanation: Cabot was born in Italy. He landed on the coast of present-day Canada.

questions.question: Which French explorer sailed up the St Lawrence River in the 1530s and claimed land for France?
questions.explanation: He heard the word 'kanata' from local people, meaning village. This word later gave Canada its name.

questions.question: Which conqueror, also called Tamerlane, ruled his empire from the city of Samarkand?
questions.explanation: He built an empire in Central Asia in the late 1300s. His descendants included the founder of the Mughal Empire.

questions.question: Which Aztec emperor met Hernán Cortés in 1519?
questions.explanation: Moctezuma welcomed Cortés into Tenochtitlan. Within two years the Spanish had taken the city.

questions.question: What did the Inca use instead of writing to keep records of numbers?
questions.explanation: These strings are called quipu. The knots showed numbers, such as counts of people or goods.

questions.question: Roald Amundsen was the first to sail through which sea route north of Canada, in 1903–06?
questions.explanation: His small ship spent three winters in the Arctic on the way. He learned from the Inuit how to dress and travel in the cold.

questions.question: Mansa Musa, who travelled to Mecca in 1324 with great amounts of gold, ruled which West African empire?
questions.explanation: He gave away so much gold on his trip that its price in Cairo fell for years.

questions.question: What was the capital of the Inca Empire?
questions.explanation: Cusco lies high in the Andes of Peru. The Spanish later built churches on top of its Inca stone walls.

questions.question: Which journalist and explorer found David Livingstone in Africa in 1871?
questions.explanation: Stanley is said to have greeted him with the words 'Dr Livingstone, I presume?'

questions.question: Most of the Ottoman Empire's heartland later became which country?
questions.explanation: The Republic of Turkey was founded in 1923. The Ottoman Empire had ruled parts of three continents.

questions.question: Which Spanish queen helped to pay for Columbus's first trip across the Atlantic?
questions.explanation: Isabella was Queen of Castile. Her marriage to Ferdinand of Aragon joined the two biggest kingdoms of Spain.

questions.question: What was the name of the ship that James Cook sailed on his first voyage around the world?
questions.explanation: Endeavour was a coal ship that the Royal Navy bought for the voyage. It was strong and had a flat bottom.

questions.question: In the 1800s, which country ruled most of India?
questions.explanation: First the British East India Company ruled, and from 1858 the British Crown took over.

questions.question: Polynesian sailors crossed huge areas of the Pacific without compasses. What did they read to find their way?
questions.explanation: They remembered the paths of stars and how waves bend around islands. In this way they settled islands far apart.

questions.question: Cook's first voyage, which left England in 1768, went to Tahiti to watch what?
questions.explanation: Astronomers wanted to measure how far away the Sun is. Cook then sailed on to New Zealand and Australia.

questions.question: Which valuable metal from mines such as Potosí made Spain rich in the 1500s?
questions.explanation: Potosí is a mountain town in what is now Bolivia. Silver coins from there were used in many countries.

questions.question: What do historians call the time, from the 1400s, when European ships explored much of the world?
questions.explanation: New ships, maps and compasses made long sea trips possible. Many of these trips led to colonies.

questions.question: Which European country ruled Java and much of what is now Indonesia for centuries?
questions.explanation: The Dutch East India Company began its rule there in the 1600s.

questions.question: Which famous river's source did British explorers such as Speke and Burton search for in the 1800s?
questions.explanation: Speke reached Lake Victoria in 1858 and said it was the source of the river.

questions.question: Which Spanish sailor captained the Victoria and brought it home in 1522, finishing the first trip around the world?
questions.explanation: Only 18 men came home on the Victoria, three years after five ships had set out.

questions.question: Which Spanish explorer was the first European to see the Pacific Ocean from the Americas, in 1513?
questions.explanation: He crossed the narrow land of Panama and called the new sea the South Sea.

questions.question: The Treaty of Tordesillas in 1494 shared newly found lands between which two countries?
questions.explanation: A line on the map gave lands to the west to Spain and lands to the east to Portugal. This is one reason why Brazil speaks Portuguese.

questions.question: Which Portuguese commander led the fleet that reached Brazil in 1500, on its way to India?
questions.explanation: His fleet sailed far out into the Atlantic to catch the winds. Cabral claimed the land for Portugal.

questions.question: Who founded the Mughal Empire after winning the Battle of Panipat in 1526?
questions.explanation: Babur came from Central Asia and was a descendant of both Timur and Genghis Khan.

questions.question: Who were the Janissaries in the Ottoman Empire?
questions.explanation: They lived in barracks and were paid by the sultan. Their name comes from Turkish words meaning 'new soldiers'.

questions.question: What was the Mongol Empire's relay system of riders and stations for carrying messages called?
questions.explanation: Riders changed horses at stations, so messages travelled very far in a short time.

questions.question: In 1258 a Mongol army led by Hulagu captured which great city?
questions.explanation: It ended the rule of the Abbasid caliphs in Baghdad, which had lasted about 500 years.

questions.question: Which Mongol state collected tribute from Russian princes from the 1200s to the 1400s?
questions.explanation: It was one of the parts the Mongol Empire split into. Moscow grew strong while it paid tribute.

questions.question: Which writer helped Marco Polo write down his travels while both were in prison in Genoa?
questions.explanation: Rustichello of Pisa was a writer of knight stories. The book was first written in a form of Old French.

questions.question: Who was the last Aztec emperor, captured by the Spanish in 1521?
questions.explanation: He came to power after Moctezuma II and then Cuitláhuac had died. The Spanish took Tenochtitlan after a long siege.

questions.question: Which small ship did Roald Amundsen use to sail through the Northwest Passage?
questions.explanation: Gjøa was a fishing boat with only seven men on board. It was small enough to sail in shallow icy water.

questions.question: What does the name of Nansen's ship Fram mean in Norwegian?
questions.explanation: Fram was built to be pushed up, not crushed, by pack ice. Later Amundsen used it to sail to Antarctica.

questions.question: Which ship carried Scott's last expedition to Antarctica in 1910?
questions.explanation: Discovery was used on Scott's first expedition. Nimrod was Shackleton's ship.

questions.question: After Endurance was lost, to which island did Shackleton sail in a small boat to get help?
questions.explanation: The boat James Caird sailed more than 1,200 kilometres from Elephant Island. Shackleton then crossed the island's mountains on foot.

questions.question: On his second voyage, James Cook became the first known person to cross which line?
questions.explanation: He crossed it in 1773 but never saw land, because it was hidden behind the ice.

questions.question: In 1958 Edmund Hillary drove to the South Pole with what?
questions.explanation: He was part of an expedition that crossed Antarctica. Hillary's tractors reached the Pole before the main team.

questions.question: Which Greenland-born explorer led a long trip across Arctic North America to Alaska in 1921–24?
questions.explanation: His mother was part Inuit, and he grew up speaking Greenlandic. On the trip he studied the culture of the Inuit.

questions.question: Who was the only member of the Danish expedition to Arabia, sent in 1761, to come home alive?
questions.explanation: King Frederik V sent scientists to explore Arabia. Niebuhr made maps that were used for many years.

questions.question: What was Genghis Khan's birth name?
questions.explanation: He took the title Genghis Khan in 1206, when a great meeting of the tribes chose him as their leader.

questions.question: In 1529 the Ottoman army besieged which European city?
questions.explanation: The siege did not succeed, because of rain and a long supply line. They tried again in 1683.

questions.question: Which dynasty ruled Persia from 1501 to 1736 and made Isfahan a grand city?
questions.explanation: The Safavids were rivals of the Ottomans for many years.

questions.question: In 1510 which city on India's west coast became the centre of Portuguese power in Asia?
questions.explanation: Portugal ruled Goa for about 450 years, until 1961.

questions.question: Which island group was known to Europeans as the Spice Islands, because cloves and nutmeg grew there?
questions.explanation: The Moluccas are now part of Indonesia. Many European countries fought to control them, because the spices were worth so much.

questions.question: Cape Horn at the tip of South America is named after a town in which country?
questions.explanation: Dutch sailors Schouten and Le Maire named it in 1616 after the town of Hoorn.

questions.question: Which African river did the Scottish explorer Mungo Park follow in 1796 and 1805?
questions.explanation: Park wanted to find where the river ended. He died on the second trip.

questions.question: Which Chinese monk travelled to India in the 600s, and inspired the story 'Journey to the West'?
questions.explanation: He travelled for about 16 years and brought home hundreds of books.

questions.question: Which Greek explorer sailed to northern Europe in the 300s BC and wrote about a land called Thule?
questions.explanation: He came from the Greek colony of Massalia, now Marseille. He wrote that summer nights in the far north were very short.

questions.question: Which British officer's lost expedition of 1845 searched for the Northwest Passage with the ships Erebus and Terror?
questions.explanation: None of his 129 men returned. The wrecks of both ships were found in 2014 and 2016.

questions.question: Which scientist explored Latin America from 1799 to 1804 and wrote about its nature?
questions.explanation: Humboldt climbed volcanoes and measured plants at different heights. Many places are named after him.

questions.question: Which explorer first sailed through the Northeast Passage, north of Russia, in 1878–79 aboard the Vega?
questions.explanation: He was born in Finland and worked in Sweden. The ship was stuck in ice for months near the Bering Strait.

questions.question: What was New York called when the Dutch ruled it?
questions.explanation: The Dutch settlement was on the island of Manhattan. The English took it in 1664.

questions.question: Which Chinese port was a Portuguese trading base from the 1500s?
questions.explanation: Portuguese traders settled there in the 1550s. Portugal handed Macau back to China in 1999.

questions.question: The Spanish Manila galleons crossed the Pacific between Manila and which port in Mexico?
questions.explanation: The ships carried silver to Asia and brought silk and spices back.

questions.question: In October 1492 Columbus first landed in the Americas on an island in which group?
questions.explanation: He called the island San Salvador. He left from the Canary Islands about five weeks earlier.

questions.question: Which mapmaker first put the name 'America' on a map, in 1507?
questions.explanation: He named the land after Amerigo Vespucci. He left the name off his later maps, but it had already caught on.

questions.question: Zheng He's first voyage began in 1405 under which Ming emperor?
questions.explanation: Yongle also moved the capital to Beijing and built the Forbidden City.

questions.question: What were the Aztec 'chinampas'?
questions.explanation: They made rich soil, and farmers could grow several harvests a year near Tenochtitlan.

questions.question: Which Dutch captain made the first recorded European landing in Australia, in 1606?
questions.explanation: He sailed the ship Duyfken along the coast of Cape York. He did not know it was a new continent.

questions.question: What does the Inca name for their empire, Tawantinsuyu, mean?
questions.explanation: The four regions met in the capital, Cusco. Roads ran out from Cusco to each of them.
